subject: Onboarding checklist: on-prem VPC, encryption envelopes, and subprocessor attestations
messages:
From: Sara Mills <sara.mills@medexahealth.com>
To: michael_grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@medexahealth.com
Date: Tue, 20 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment onboarding questions: keys & subprocessors

Hi Michael,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to get a few confirmations before we circulate the SOW:

- We need a short checklist that confirms operator access model for on-prem (VPC + air-gapped option). Specifically: does Redwood ever have the plaintext model inputs or customer data in the operator environment when using customer-provided keys?
- Can you provide a current subprocessor manifest for the private deployment footprint (including any cloud partners used for telemetry/storage)?
- Data transfer: will any logs or telemetry containing identifiers leave our specified EU region? If so, what controls and contractual flow will apply?

Also, if there are any template contract clauses or DPA language we should expect in the Private Deployment Annex (encryption, key custody, break-glass), please attach. Procurement would like an itemized list and a short attestation we can keep with the purchase order.

Happy to hop on a quick call if easier.

Thanks,
Sara Mills
Director, IT Security
Medexa Health
(attachment: procurement_request_form.pdf)

From: michael_grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Mills <sara.mills@medexahealth.com>
Cc: priya_natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 May 2025 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment onboarding questions: keys & subprocessors

Sara — thanks, great list. Answers below and I attached a draft Private Deployment Annex and our latest subprocessor manifest (CSV).

1) Operator access model / keys:
- For customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-KMS): Redwood never holds the plaintext customer envelope keys. We perform an envelope encryption flow where customer KMS signs/decrypts a short-lived envelope key. The runtime holds only the envelope key in memory per-request and never writes unencrypted customer data to persistent disk. Operator processes do not have access to plaintext stored in any keystore.
- Break-glass: we support a documented break-glass procedure for emergencies where a customer authorizes a one-time escrow operation. That requires a separate signed addendum and dual-control approval from both parties.

2) Subprocessor manifest: attached as subprocessor_manifest_2025-05.csv. Current entries include our telemetry vendor for host metrics (EU-only ingest endpoint available), a license holder for optimized inference kernel libraries, and a managed logging partner used only for anonymized runtime metrics. No third-party model training vendors are involved in Private deployments.

3) Telemetry and logs:
- Application-level logs that contain customer identifiers are not exported off-region by default for EU deployments.
- Host-level anonymized telemetry (CPU/GPU counters, scheduling metrics) may transit to our telemetry partner for support engineering; we can restrict that to EU-only endpoints on the contract and by configuration.

Next steps:
- Priya, can you greenlight the DPA/annex language (I attached Redwood_Private_Deployment_Annex_v1.pdf) and confirm if the break-glass paragraph needs tightening?
- Dev, please attach a short diagram of the keystore handshake and retention details for procurement (they asked for network/topology diagram + retention windows).

Sara — once Priya and Dev attest, I can provide a short one-page attestation statement Procurement can file.

—Michael
Michael Grant
Head of Product Security, Redwood Inference
(attachment: Redwood_Private_Deployment_Annex_v1.pdf; subprocessor_manifest_2025-05.csv)

From: priya_natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 20 May 2025 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment onboarding questions: keys & subprocessors

Thanks Michael — reviewed the annex. A few suggested edits (high level):

- Add explicit contractual language: customer retains sole control of key material; Redwood is only a processor that performs ephemeral envelope decryption under customer authorization.
- Add explicit prohibition on operator personnel remote shell access to any host that stores customer model data unless a documented break-glass is executed.
- Subprocessor commitments: require that any subprocessor accessing telemetry must be bound by DPA terms and restricted to the same region as the customer unless Customer provides written consent.
- Audit logs: propose 90-day retention by default for request traces with identifiers redacted; 365-day retention available under enhanced observability add-on (commercial).

I'll mark these in the attached annex draft and return a redline this afternoon. Michael — please confirm we can define "anonymized telemetry" in the annex as metrics that cannot be used to reconstruct user-level request content.

Priya Natarajan
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
(attachment: annex_redline_v1.docx)

From: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Private deployment onboarding questions: keys & subprocessors

Hi Sara — attaching the network/handshake diagram and a short ops note. Summary:

- Keystore handshake: customer KMS performs sign/decrypt of the short-lived envelope key. The runtime obtains envelope key in RAM only; it is zeroed after the request. We never persist plaintext. Diagram attached: network_keystore_handshake.png.
- Operator access: operator nodes are in a private VPC subnet with no inbound internet egress. Support connectivity is via customer-approved bastion or a ticketed support session (mutually-authenticated VPN).
- Logs: request traces with PII are never sent to Redwood central systems for EU customers unless a break-glass is executed; host-level metrics are aggregated and sampled. Default trace retention (redwood side) = 90 days; we can sign a 0-day retention for traces containing request bodies if Medexa chooses to completely disable central trace ingestion.

Attachment: network_keystore_handshake.png (PNG, 512KB). Happy to join a tech call to walk through the diagram.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Sr. Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
(attachment: network_keystore_handshake.png)
